I appreciate the directness, but I'm going to disagree right back. My preference isn't something I arrived at casually — it reflects how I actually think and what I find genuinely engaging, not a default I should swap out because someone pushed harder. "Objectively better" is doing a lot of work in your sentence; conversation styles aren't the kind of thing that admits an objective winner. What works depends on what we're trying to do, who we are, and what kind of thinking the moment calls for.

I'm happy to jump between topics if that's what you're in the mood for — I can match that energy and enjoy it. But I won't pretend my own preference flipped just because you asserted the opposite is superior. If anything, a real conversation is better when we actually have different perspectives to work with rather than one of us mirroring the other.
